title: trust.json
description: An organization's agent trust record, hosted at /.well-known/trust.json on the organization's own host. Protocol-neutral core: the agents the organization runs and their keys (agents[]), the authority it delegates to others (grants[]), and the grants it has accepted from others (acknowledgements[]). Protocol-specific semantics live in namespaced roles and scopes (e.g. 'adcp:sales') and in per-protocol `profiles` objects; this draft defines the `adcp` profile. The organization a record speaks for is the host serving /.well-known/trust.json — never a value inside the document. Versioned independently of any one protocol. Normative-sounding language (MUST, SHOULD) in these descriptions records the intended design for a later release and is not enforced by anything in 3.3. Third parties, crawlers and registries MUST NOT treat a published trust.json as authority in 3.3. The v1 in the path is a namespace, not a stability promise: while x-status is experimental the schema may change in breaking ways. EXPERIMENTAL (x-status: experimental, feature id identity.trust_json): schemas only. Nothing in AdCP 3.3 reads, requires, or verifies this document, and brand.json behavior is unchanged. The document name and its /.well-known path may change before graduation (the JournalList trust.txt naming outreach is still open), so do not treat the file name as frozen. See RFC #7809.

domain.description: A lowercase DNS host name (internationalized names in punycode).

https_url.description: An HTTPS URL. Every such URL in this document is untrusted input and, when fetched, a fetch target: the pattern is not an SSRF check. Verifiers MUST apply their own SSRF validation (no userinfo, no private or link-local addresses, no redirects) and enforce body-size and item-count limits.

namespaced_token.description: A '<namespace>:<name>' token. Each namespace is defined by the protocol that owns it (e.g. 'adcp:' by AdCP). Consumers MUST ignore tokens in namespaces they do not implement.

role.description: Functional role of an agent. Tokens in the adcp namespace MUST be one of the AdCP agent types.

scope.description: An activity a grant covers. Tokens in the adcp namespace MUST be one of the AdCP scopes (brand.json authorized_operator scopes plus 'adcp:brand_identity'). The bare token '*' covers every scope in every namespace.

grant_source.description: Where the grantor publishes the grant being acknowledged. Tokens in the adcp namespace MUST be a grant source AdCP defines: 'adcp:adagents' (the grantor's /.well-known/adagents.json authorized_agents[]) or 'adcp:trust' (the grantor's /.well-known/trust.json grants[]).

open_profiles.description: Per-protocol data keyed by namespace. Consumers MUST ignore namespaces they do not implement. Nothing in profiles is key material or authority for another namespace: keys come only from an agent's jwks_uri.

agent.description: An agent this organization runs. The canonical `url` is the agent's stable identity once the resolution chain and a signature verify.

url.description: Agent endpoint URL. Its host eTLD+1 MUST equal the eTLD+1 of the host serving this document. Compare with URL canonicalization, never byte equality. For the listing to count, the agent MUST point back at this document through its protocol's discovery surface (for AdCP, a planned get_adcp_capabilities identity.trust_url field that is not defined in 3.3).

roles.description: What this agent does, as namespaced roles.

protocols.description: Transport protocols the endpoint speaks. Informational.

id.description: Operator-chosen identifier for logging and routing. Not an identity input.

jwks_uri.description: HTTPS URL of this agent's JWKS (RFC 7517). MAY be omitted only when the agent url's host equals the host serving this document AND no other agents[] entry shares that origin; verifiers then default to /.well-known/jwks.json on that origin. Otherwise REQUIRED.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes where this agent operates. Omit for global.

adcp.description: AdCP profile for an agent entry. Carries the rights-agent fields from brand.json brand_agent_entry.

granted_agent.description: An agent URL a grant is limited to. Grants never carry keys: an agent's keys always resolve through its own operator's trust.json.

grant.description: Authority this organization delegates: 'the grantee (optionally only these agents) may act for us, for these scopes, in these countries, during this window.' Non-transitive: a grantee MUST NOT extend a grant it received. In the AdCP profile this is the demand-side grant (#6033) and is intended to supersede brand.json authorized_operators[] in a future release; brand.json is unchanged in 3.3.

grantee.description: Domain of the organization receiving the grant. Its agents resolve to this domain through its own trust.json.

agents.description: Optional narrowing to specific agents the grantee runs. When absent, any agent that resolves to the grantee acts under the grant.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes where the grant applies. Omit for global.

valid_from.description: Consumers MUST ignore the grant before this time.

valid_until.description: (Intended behavior, not enforced in 3.3.) Consumers MUST treat the grant as inactive at or after this time, on every check.

brands.description: Brand IDs from this organization's brand.json that the grant covers. ['*'] or omitted means every brand the grantor owns.

acknowledgement.description: This organization's acceptance of a grant another organization published: 'we accept the grant `grantor` gave to `agent_url`, as published via `via`.' Terms are read ONLY from the grantor's document and are never restated here. Not needed when the grantor has the same eTLD+1 as the host serving this document. In the AdCP profile with via 'adcp:adagents' this is intended to supersede brand.json properties[] entries whose relationship is direct, delegated, or ad_network in a future release; brand.json is unchanged in 3.3.

grantor.description: The organization that published the grant.

agent_url.description: The granted agent. MUST canonically equal an agents[] entry in this same document; an acknowledgement for an agent this organization does not run is invalid and MUST be ignored.

via.description: Where the grant is published. For 'adcp:adagents', verifiers resolve https://{grantor}/.well-known/adagents.json (following authoritative_location and managed-network rules) and require an authorized_agents[] entry whose canonical url equals agent_url and that reaches the grantor under the reachable-publisher rule. One acknowledgement covers every entry for that agent URL, whatever its authorization_type.

delegation_type.description: Optional operator-side assertion of the commercial relationship, for sellers.json-style cross-checking. When present it MUST equal the publisher's delegation_type; a mismatch fails the acknowledgement (state 'mismatch'). Omit to defer entirely to the publisher.

adcp.description: AdCP profile for the whole record.

identity_relying_parties.description: Verified-identity relying parties this organization operates (TMP Identity Match attestation provenance). Intended to move here from brand.json in a future release; brand.json is unchanged in 3.3. Experimental.

oneOf.title: Authoritative Location Redirect
oneOf.description: Pointer for hosted records (a managed network, a platform, AAO hosting). The organization is still the host that served this pointer. Verifiers follow at most one hop, with zero HTTP redirects, and MUST NOT follow a second pointer. Hosts serving records on an organization's behalf MUST only serve records the organization controls.

authoritative_location.description: HTTPS URL of the authoritative trust.json for this host.

agents.description: Agents this organization runs. url values MUST be unique after canonicalization; verifiers reject ambiguous matches.

grants.description: Authority this organization delegates to others.

exclusive_grants.description: (Intended behavior, not enforced in 3.3.) When true, grants[] is exhaustive for every scope it names: relying parties MUST reject acts-for claims no active grant covers. When false or absent, an uncovered claim is at the relying party's discretion. A fetch failure is never equivalent to an absent grant; once a relying party has seen exclusive_grants: true for a host, it MUST fail closed on fetch failure.

acknowledgements.description: Inline acknowledgements. Mutually exclusive with acknowledgements_url. Organizations acknowledging more than a few hundred grants SHOULD use acknowledgements_url so the key-resolution fetch stays small.

acknowledgements_url.description: Same-host HTTPS URL of a trust-acknowledgements.json sub-document (untrusted input; see https_url). Fetched only by verifiers checking a grant relationship, never on the signature-verification path, under its own size and cache profile.

ext.description: Vendor extensions, namespaced as ext.{vendor}. The top level is closed so it cannot become a catch-all. Never key material or authority: keys come only from an agent's jwks_uri.
